# History List Scope

## How To Build

A HistoryListScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A HistoryListScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

A way back to everything sent before of one kind, such as previous tasks or previous answers: a small row that expands into a list of every one of them.

### Shape

#### Description

The same row and list, looking and behaving the same, wherever something sent before can be looked back on. Each use names what it lists, what the row counts, and what the row reads while expanded.

#### Row

A small row, always shown where it is used, with the tab bar's background colour. It reads "No …", "1 …", or "N …" followed by what it counts, beside a chevron, and does nothing until there is anything to list. Clicking it expands the list, and the row then reads what it says to go back; clicking it again closes the list.

#### List

A scrollable accordion of every item, oldest first, with a [ScrollbarScope](../scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope). Each time it is expanded, it opens scrolled to the bottom, with the most recent items in view, however it was scrolled when last closed, the first time as much as any other, and whether it takes the place of the latest task or slides up as a drawer. Each is headed by its status and the first line of its prompt, with a Resend button at its right, when the use offers one, and opens onto the compiled prompt it was sent as and its [TaskTableScope](../task-table/index.md#task-table-scope). One item is open at a time. A use can say its tables collapse the steps leading up to the result, as previous answers do; previous tasks show their tables whole.
An open item is exactly as wide as the list, however long the lines in its prompt or table, which wrap rather than running past the list's edge, and exactly as tall as what it shows: it ends a small margin below its table, like the margin above its prompt, with no empty space beneath it before the next item or the end of the list.
However long an open item's output, the list lays out only what is in

##### View

an open item's prompt, its table's header, and each of its

table's rows are drawn as the list scrolls to them, as each item's heading is.

The labels are readable in both light and dark mode.
.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.md:51:The header for the latest task is coloured like the tab the task was sent from, the colour of its mode, of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope), as the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) body shows for that tab. A task from the history that doesn't say which tab it was sent from keeps the tab bar's colour. The queue along the bottom and the previous tasks row along the top both have the same background colour as the tab bar.
.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.md:70:However long the list of previous tasks grows, drawing it costs no more than drawing the tasks in view, so scrolling, animations, and new output stay smooth.

From top to bottom it holds the previous tasks row, the header for the latest task, the latest task's output, and the queue.
.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/index.md:28:#### Chat History
.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/index.md:32:#### Previous Tasks
.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/index.md:34:Previous tasks are a [HistoryListScope](../../ui/components/history-list/index.md#history-list-scope) along the top of the view, listing every task sent. Its row counts every task but the latest, which heads the view: "No previous tasks", "1 previous task", or "N previous tasks", and each offers Resend. Expanded, the list takes the place of the latest task and its output, and the row reads "Back to the latest task".
.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/index.md:35:Every task in the list has a checkbox at the left of its heading, before its status, and clicking it selects or deselects the task without opening or closing it. Shift-clicking one selects every task between it and the one last clicked, never deselecting any; with none clicked before, it selects or deselects that one as a plain click does. The selection is kept while the list is closed and opened again, until it is cleared or sent. Each open project keeps its own, as the [OpenProjectsScope](../open-projects/index.md#open-projects-scope) says. Previous answers have no checkboxes.
.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/index.md:37:A batch action sends each of its tasks to the other mode, as the [PromptSendingScope](./sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says for one, oldest first: the first starts straight away while the harness is free and the rest queue behind it, so they run in the order they were first sent, each saved in the history as a new task. Once sent, the tasks it sent are deselected, the rest of the selection is kept, and the list stays as it was, still expanded, with nothing opened. With no project open, it sends nothing, a notification says a project must be opened first, and the selection is kept.
.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/index.md:46:Beside the latest task's Resend button, a small ghost button with a code icon, whose tooltip says "View the raw prompt", opens a modal showing exactly what the harness was given for the task, once it has been sent: nothing rendered, nothing hidden. Clicking it never opens or closes anything else in the header. Until the task has compiled, it is disabled, its tooltip reading "No prompt sent yet". Only the latest task's header has it; previous tasks and answers don't.
.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/index.md:58:What it shows is what was sent, not what the templates say now: the system prompt as sent, and the harness it was sent to, are saved in the task's history record beside its compiled user prompt, for questions as much as tasks, and for a harness given one combined text, the system prompt alone, the combined text built again from it exactly as it was sent, so the modal shows the same for a task restored from the history. A task saved before this was recorded shows its system prompt as "Not recorded".
.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/index.md:72:#### History
.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/index.md:74:Every task sent is saved in the prompt history with the project's data, as the [ProjectDataScope](../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, and its record once its run is over. Opening the project, the first time in a launch, brings back every task in order, with its output replayed from that record. The record keeps each message sent to the task while it ran, as typed and as compiled, in its place among the lines the harness printed, so the task comes back as the exchange it was, each message a Sent row followed by what came of it. A task with no record shows as "Not recorded".

The Previous tasks list is now grouped by session. The first task of each session gets a small muted "Session N" label with a line under it, numbered from the oldest. I haven't opened the app to look at it.

- **How a session is decided:** each task now remembers the conversation id the harness reports for it. For tasks loaded from history, that id comes from their saved record. A new group starts wherever the conversation changes.
- **Tasks with no known session:** tasks with no record (shown as "Not recorded"), or that stopped before the harness reported a conversation, stay in the group before them. A still-running task that starts a new conversation moves into its own group as soon as the harness reports it.
- **Previous answers** aren't grouped. Grouping is an option on the list, and only Previous tasks has it turned on.
- The list still only draws the rows in view, so long histories stay smooth.

**Tests:** I added `previous_tasks_group_by_session`, which checks where groups start, and it passes; so do the other history tests. The full suite has 6 failures:
- **Five from last time:** the three prompt-wording tests (in `hidden_anchor.rs` and `system_prompts.rs`), plus `code_tasks_sent_to_spec_are_told_what_the_code_task_did` and `batch_sent_tasks_run_in_order_in_the_other_mode`.
- **`long_output_is_measured_a_few_rows_a_frame`:** new this run, but it passed both times I ran it on its own. It looks timing-sensitive when the whole suite runs at once.

The spec doesn't mention session groups yet (`spec/scope/prompt-mode/index.pi` and the history-list spec), so it will need updating to match. This turn's constraints are in `.suspense/history/1790707075-Prompt_0417ddca7e70cded.understanding.md`.
